textbookText: 2. Sexual phase of Plasmodium vivax in female Anopheles mosquito a. Sucking up blood by the mosquito Female Anopheles mosquito sucks blood of malaria infected person with gametocytes and other phases of this parasite in RBCs. In the alimentary canal of mosquito, Gametocytes remain undigested because they have developed adaptation against digestive enzymes of the mosquito. b. Gametogony (Development of gametes) Gametogony is the process of development of male and female gametes from gametocytes. Microgametocytes give rise to the formation of male gametes or microgametes. In this process, microgametocytes in the stomach of mosquito undergo ex-flagellation process, which is favoured by the sudden fall in temperature as the microgametocytes are transferred from warm blooded human to cold-blooded mosquito. During this process, nucleus of microgametocyte divides by mitosis and produce about 6-8 haploid nuclei which lie in the periphery of cytoplasm and then cytoplasm along with each nucleus is projected out in the form of flagellar structure. Each projection separates as a mature and motile male gamete.
Similarly, macrogametocyte undergoes some structural re-organization and grows into a nonmotile gamete called female gamete or ovum.

Do you know? According to Bano (1959), only the zygote in Plasmodium is diploid, while all stages of life cycle, including gametes, are haploid. It is so because the zygote initially divides by meiosis. c. Fertilization and ookinete formation: The macrogamete or female gamete develops a small protuberance or outgrowth called receptive cone which is to receive micro-gamete or male gamete at the time of fertilization. Many microgametes approach the female gamete but only one of them is able to enter the macrogamete or ovum by penetrating the receptive cone. Fertilization takes place to form zygote and this process is also called syngamy.
Questions to think? What is the difference between syngamy and synkaryon?

Zygote remains rounded and motionless for about 24 hours and then gets elongated to become a motile worm like (vermiform) structure called ookinete or vermicule which measure about 15µ-20µ in length and 3 µ in breadth. d. Encystment and sporogony Ookinete penetrates the wall of stomach of mosquito and it remains attached beneath the outer epithelial layer of stomach. Then, it becomes spherical and undergoes encystment by developing a thin, elastic, membranous cyst wall. The cyst wall is secreted by ookinete itself and with some tissues of stomach of mosquito. The encysted ookinete is now referred as oocyst. About 50 or more oocysts can be seen on the stomach of an infected mosquito. Sporogony is the process of asexual multiplication to form sporozoites in the oocyst. In this process, the nucleus first divides by meiosis and, subsequently, by mitosis to form several haploid daughter nuclei. Meanwhile, cytoplasm also develops many large vacuoles making it sponge like appearance. Numerous cytoplasmic masses are also formed that take up individual nuclei. Then, each cytoplasmic mass along with a daughter nucleus and vacuoles give rise to a slender, spindle shaped haploid cell called a sporozoite. A mature oocyst may contain about 10,000 sporozoites. Each sporozoite is a sickle shaped structure which is pointed at the ends and broad at the middle bearing a large prominent nucleus with other cell organelles in cytoplasm. By the rupture of mature oocyst, sporozoites are released into haemocoelom or body cavity of the Anopheles mosquito, from where they reach the salivary gland and enter the duct of hypopharynx to be discharged with saliva while biting a healthy human. Then, another asexual phase of life cycle continues in human.

Plasmodium falciparum is worldwide in distribution. It is mainly distributed in tropical, subtropical and warmer regions of the world. It causes malignant tertian malaria or pernicious malaria fever almost continuously or at the interval of about 2 days. It causes a serious condition in human called Blackwater fever which is characterized by the complete destruction of RBCs and haematuria (discharging the characteristic black or dark coloured urine). It is most dangerous species of Plasmodium that causes cerebral malaria. Death rate is higher in the infection of P. falciparum.
